rule: This map is read-only until the Wave 4 restatement. It states every non-test file outside the relation fence that still names a dying engine surface, the symbols it names, and the declared surface that answers it after the cut. Symbols are resolved from the syntax tree, not by text match, so a name that appears only in a string literal or a comment is not a read. A consumer reading only a surviving restatement target is not listed: it is already at its post-cut home. A consumer whose distinction no owner publishes carries a gap identity rather than an invented column; a gap is a finding to close in the owner, never in the consumer.

gaps.distinction: every published query answer, at the canonical snapshot the read paths already read
gaps.detail: The read side is already where the cut wants it: these consumers call analysis/snapshot.Query against a sealed snapshot and use the engine only to open the answer. What has no successor is the write side. The only non-test code that publishes into a canonical snapshot is analysis/engine/publication_column.go - PutColumn at line 271, DeclareQuery at 283, SetRow at 292 - and S6-engine-publication-reads deletes it. Nothing under analysis/relation, analysis/engine/relation or domain/*/relation imports analysis/snapshot at all. So S8-read-paths restates five packages onto "analysis/snapshot read laws with no analysis/engine import" and the snapshot they are to read has, after the cut, nobody to fill it. Relation rows are also not addressable from a sealed artifact by column identity: snapshot.Read is keyed by an Axis slot, not a model.ColumnID, and relbindgen addresses inputs by slot ordinal against a live frame. Publishing is the blocker; reading is not.

gaps.distinction: none - the distinction is published, by the relation-side operation instead
gaps.detail: domain/static/type_summary_observation.go exports AccumulateTypeSummary over engine.OrderedCells[TypeFact] and nothing calls it. The live fold is domain/static/relation/operation.go, whose StaticTypeSummaryOperation.Evaluate calls AccumulateTypeSummaryRows with argument.Cells. The family is bound in the corpus as StaticTypeSummary with output column static-type-summary. This entry is therefore not work for W4 but a deletion the cut can take: it is recorded because S6-domain-observation-restatement lists the file for restatement, and restating a reducer nobody calls would be work spent on residue.

domain/typestate/statecell/generated_relation_owner.go imports analysis/engine/execution, which S2-engine-execution deletes, and it belongs to no manifest entry. Its eight siblings are all named in S3-generated-relation-owners. The typestate family is bound in the corpus, so this is a hole in the delete-set rather than an unbound judgment: the cut as written would delete every generated relation owner except this one and leave it naming a package that is gone.

gaps.distinction: the scalar row templates a workspace artifact product reads
gaps.detail: analysis/internal/workspace/artifact_products.go is the only surviving non-test consumer of analysis/engine/rows and rows/scalarlower. Those packages are retained under K-engine-rows as keep-if-generic, and the manifest rule is that an undischarged obligation is a delete. The obligation is undischarged at this ref, so whether this consumer has a surface after the cut is not yet decided. It is recorded so the decision is made rather than defaulted.

gaps.distinction: a production entry into the declared rule surface: the lowering from an authored declaration to the canonical ExecutionSchema that every declared-surface consumer is to read its answer out of after the cut
gaps.detail: relcompile holds the grammar and the name registry - Declaration, Rule, JoinSpec, Operand, Publication, Registry and Compile - and lowers them to plan.ExecutionSchema. What it does not hold is a way in from production: no non-test file in the tree imports it, so the whole surface is reachable only from the census and law tests that pin it. Measured against the sixteen entries that name it as their target, it declares none of the thirty-seven symbols they read; every one of those symbols is declared in analysis/engine and nowhere else, so no partial move exists either. No manifest entry builds the entry point: S1-analyzer-constructor restates the constructor onto analysis/engine/relation/runtime, and the S4, S6 and S8 entries that own these consumers all restate onto surfaces of their own. Until an authored declaration can be compiled and read from production code, a consumer pointed here can only be bridged, which is why the map states the prerequisite instead of the move.

gaps.distinction: the composed and solved target the analyzer constructor and the runtime-composition readers are restated onto
gaps.detail: analysis/engine/relation/runtime holds one file, doc.go. It declares no exported identity and no non-test file imports it. S1-analyzer-constructor is blocked_by nothing and is the entry the manifest says runs before every deletion, so the order the cut is planned in makes it first; it is unreachable all the same, because the surface it restates onto is a stub. The four consumers that name it read CommittedProgram and Answer, both declared in analysis/engine alone.
